content: 1. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Cobicistat and clarithromycin mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases cobicistat levels, and cobicistat increases darunavir levels. Avoid or use alternatives. 3. Darunavir increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If coadministration is necessary, reduce colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. Colchicine is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 4. Darunavir decreases conjugated estrogen levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Darunavir and cobicistat both increase copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 6. Cobicistat increases crizotinib levels, potentially causing QT prolongation. Avoid or use alternatives. If unavoidable, reduce crizotinib dose to 250 mg daily. 7. Darunavir and cobicistat increase dabrafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. Dabrafenib decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternatives. 8. Cobicistat and darunavir increase daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 9. Cobicistat increases dexamethasone levels, while dexamethasone decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. Long-term corticosteroid use with CYP3A4 metabolism may lead to systemic effects like Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. 10. Cobicistat increases dihydroergotamine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Darunavir increases dofetilide levels, raising the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid or use alternatives. 12. Cobicistat increases doxorubicin and liposomal doxorubicin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 13. Darunavir increases edoxaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use alternatives. Dose adjustments may be required for DVT/PE treatment (reduce to 30 mg daily). No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 14. Efavirenz decreases darunavir and cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. Coadministration may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance. 15. Cobicistat and darunavir increase elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 16. Cobicistat and darunavir increase elbasvir/grazoprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Darunavir and cobicistat increase encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. If unavoidable, reduce encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 18. Darunavir and cobicistat increase entrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Darunavir increases enzalutamide levels, while enzalutamide decreases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 20. Cobicistat increases erdafitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 21. Darunavir increases ergoloid mesylates levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Cobicistat and erythromycin base mutually increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative antibiotics. 23. Darunavir increases erythromycin base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. 24. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for virologic response. 25. Darunavir decreases conjugated synthetic estrogen levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternatives. 26. Cobicistat increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 27. Cobicistat increases etravirine levels, while etravirine decreases cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 28. Etravirine decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 29. Darunavir and cobicistat increase everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 30. Darunavir and cobicistat increase fedratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce fedratinib dose to 200 mg daily. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase fedratinib dose to 300 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 400 mg daily as tolerated. 31. Darunavir and cobicistat increase felbamate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. 32. Cobicistat increases fentanyl transdermal and transmucosal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl dose as needed. 33. Darunavir decreases fexinidazole levels, while fexinidazole increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternatives. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects with CYP3A4 substrates.
